title: Daily Pump Insulin for Cartridge Refills: Insulin Pump Program Clinical Questions
content:
**How does a recent prescription on the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program affect the daily pump insulin behind a cartridge or reservoir refill on an Insulin Pump Program?**
Where a written order dated in the three months before the ship date is on the active pump-delivery insulin pharmacy program — the customer's active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump — the standard window is replaced with the newest pump insulin dispensing, its insulin divided by its own supply days.

**And when there is no recent order and the pump insulin item was not dispensed recently?**
Where no such order is on file and the program's pump insulin item — J1817 on the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program and rapid-acting 10 mL vials on any other tier — was not dispensed in the three months before the ship date but was in the six months before it, the standard window is replaced with those six months, their insulin divided by the supply days they cover.

**And otherwise?**
The standard window stands.

**What counts as "in the three months" or "in the six months"?**
An order or a dispensing whose date is later than the same day of the month three or six months before the ship date.

| Insulin pharmacy records (hypothetical) | Daily pump insulin |
|---|---|
| Order 1 month old; newest dispensing 2,400 units for 30 days | replaced with 80 units a day |
| No order in 3 months; item not dispensed in 3 months; 6,000 units dispensed 5 months ago over 60 days | replaced with 100 units a day |
| No order in 3 months; item dispensed within the last 3 months | the standard window stands |
